full_judgment: 4. It was argued by the pre-emptor-respondents in the High Court Division, as the Division Bench noted, that the trial Court misunderstood section 85(2) of the NAT Act and failed to notice that a Full Bench of the then Dhaka High Court held in the case of Haji Aktaruzzaman vs. Jadunath Pal and another, 17 DLR 384, that the right of pre-emption under section 24 of the NAT Act has not been taken away by section 85(2). The High Court Division also noted the submission of the appellant, namely, that a plain reading of section 85(2) shows that the legislature meant to exclude land held by a tenant directly under the Government from the operation of the NAT Act. The appellant relied upon the cases of Munshi Golam Hossain Haji vs. Mohammad Abdul Hafez, 7 DLR 116, and Abdur Rahim vs. Sayeed Miah, 33 DLR 10. The appellant further submitted that if section 85(2) is read along with section 81A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, shortly the SAT Act, then it will be clear that the provisions of the NAT Act are not applicable to a non-agricultural tenant who has not become a tenant under the Government due to acquisition of rent-receiving interest of his landlord.
